skill.name: docker-k8s
skill.description: Create security-focused Docker and Kubernetes configurations for production cloud-native applications.

skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, or defensive container examples. Two outbound build-scan URL findings remain confirmed at low severity, and semantic review found risky Kubernetes guidance: overbroad secrets RBAC and unconstrained image tag updates.

remediation.issue: Dockerfile example performs a build-time request to an external scan URL.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the outbound build-time scan call or replace it with an explicit, user-configured scanner step that documents the destination and trust model.

remediation.issue: Kubernetes ClusterRole grants secrets access and is bound to the default ServiceAccount.
remediation.suggestion: Remove secrets from the general application ClusterRole and bind narrowly scoped roles to a dedicated ServiceAccount per workload.

remediation.issue: ArgoCD image updater example allows any image tag.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tags to a signed release pattern and pair automated updates with image verification policy.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Kubernetes Secrets RBAC
semantic_findings.description: The ClusterRole grants get, list, and watch access to secrets and binds it to the default ServiceAccount in the production namespace. Copying this pattern could expose Kubernetes secrets to workloads that do not need them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The manifest explicitly includes secrets in ClusterRole resources and binds the role to the default ServiceAccount. This is a clear least-privilege violation in Kubernetes RBAC guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Unconstrained ArgoCD Image Tag Updates
semantic_findings.description: The ArgoCD image updater example allows any image tag pattern. This can weaken deployment control if copied into production GitOps automation without tag restrictions or signature policy.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allow-tags argument contains a wildcard in the GitOps image updater configuration. The risk depends on surrounding image trust controls, but the example is unsafe as general production guidance.

content.user_title: Deploy Secure Docker and Kubernetes Workloads
content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable container and Kubernetes patterns that reduce production security risk. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code generate hardened Dockerfiles, manifests, GitOps examples, and observability guidance.
actual_capabilities: Drafts multi-stage Dockerfile patterns with non-root users and minimized runtime images.
Provides Kubernetes namespace, RBAC, deployment, network policy, and service account examples.
Explains zero-trust Kubernetes deployment concepts such as Pod Security Standards and default-deny networking.
Shows GitOps application structure for ArgoCD-style production deployments.
Includes monitoring and alerting examples for Kubernetes workloads.
Offers a production checklist covering container, network, secrets, compliance, and observability controls.
limitations: Examples require review before use in a real cluster because several values are placeholders.
It does not inspect a live Docker image, Kubernetes cluster, or cloud account.
Some Kubernetes APIs and annotations may need updates for specific cluster versions.
Security recommendations must be adapted to each organization’s threat model and compliance needs.

use_cases.title: Harden a new service deployment
use_cases.description: Generate a secure Dockerfile and Kubernetes manifest baseline for a new application before production review.

use_cases.title: Prepare GitOps deployment patterns
use_cases.description: Create ArgoCD-oriented deployment examples with sync policy, namespace targeting, and operational annotations.

use_cases.title: Review cloud-native security controls
use_cases.description: Use the checklist and examples to discuss container, RBAC, networking, observability, and secrets controls.

prompt_templates.title: Create a secure Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a secure multi-stage Dockerfile for my application. Explain the main security choices in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Kubernetes baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create Kubernetes manifests for a production service with namespace labels, deployment security context, probes, resources, and default-deny networking.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an existing deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Dockerfile and Kubernetes manifests for container security, RBAC scope, network policy, secrets handling, and observability gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a GitOps rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a secure GitOps rollout for a Kubernetes service, including ArgoCD sync settings, image update policy, monitoring alerts, and rollback considerations.

output_examples.input: Create a secure deployment baseline for a Python API.
output: A multi-stage container build plan with a non-root runtime user.
A Kubernetes deployment outline with probes, resource limits, and security context.
A network policy approach that starts from default deny rules.

output_examples.input: Review my Kubernetes manifest for risky permissions.
output: A prioritized list of RBAC, service account, and secret handling concerns.
Concrete changes to reduce privileges and isolate workloads.
Notes on which findings require cluster-specific validation.

output_examples.input: Plan GitOps deployment controls for production.
output: A rollout structure for ArgoCD-managed applications.
Recommended tag, sync, and rollback controls.
Monitoring alerts and runbook topics to support operations.

best_practices: Replace placeholder repositories, domains, identities, and secrets with organization-approved values before deployment.
Review generated RBAC, network policy, and image update rules with least privilege in mind.
Validate manifests against the target Kubernetes version and admission policies before applying them.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example manifests directly into production without security and platform review.
Do not grant secrets access to broad roles or default service accounts.
Do not allow automated image updates from unrestricted tag patterns or unverified registries.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example configurations. A user or automation tool must apply any generated manifests.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, and can guide file edits in compatible coding agents.

faq.question: Is the output ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Treat the output as a strong starting point that needs review, testing, and environment-specific changes.

faq.question: What Kubernetes topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers namespaces, RBAC, deployments, probes, security contexts, network policies, service mesh, GitOps, and monitoring examples.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare secure patterns, but a qualified reviewer should validate permissions, secrets, and deployment controls.

faq.question: Why are placeholders important?
faq.answer: Placeholders prevent accidental use of real infrastructure values. Replace them with approved internal values before testing.
